alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 23 at 11:21AM MDT until September 25 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, San Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains.

* WHEN...Through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The ground remains saturated from recent heavy rainfall over the
past week. Deep moisture has returned to southwest Colorado, with
a few inches of rainfall possible today through Thursday. In
addition, multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms are
expected today through Thursday evening producing periods of
heavy rainfall and potential flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

afd.snippet: 000 FXUS65 KGJT 231909 AFDGJT Area Forecast Discussion National Weather Service Grand Junction CO 109 PM MDT Wed Sep 23 2026 .KEY MESSAGES... - Periods of moderate to heavy rain will impact southern Colorado the next few days with drier conditions across the north and far West. - Widespread rainfall amounts in excess of an inch to over 2 inches in some areas could lead to flooding across the south

fwf.snippet: .DISCUSSION...South through southwesterly flow will keep the moisture tap in place as showers and storms continue across the region today. Showers and thunderstorms will develop along the higher terrain along and north of I-70, with frequent lightning and gusty winds expected. alerts.title: US 160 Pagosa Springs Reconstruction-147575
alerts.description: Between US 84 and Pike Drive (Pagosa Springs) from Mile Point 144.3 to Mile Point 141.8. Road construction. Starting Friday at 7:00AM MDT until Friday, at about 6:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • September 25, 7:00AM - September 25, 6:00PM Comment: Harman Park & Piedra Road-Work is underway at this intersection of US 160. Working hours will be intermittent day and night so motorists should plan for potential delays, Monday-Saturday. Please allow extra time to get through the work zone. Safety benefits of this work includes pedestrian safety upgrades and ADA accessibility improvements. Expect lane shifts and up to 15-minute delays. Crews will switch two-way traffic into the eastbound lanes, perform temporary striping operations and begin asphalt milling in the westbound lanes. Parking will not be permitted on US 160 and vehicles will be towed at the owner's expense. Westbound lane closures, 10’ width and 75’ length restrictions will remain in place 24/7 through end of 2026. Work is weather-dependent. For questions contact the project team at 970-335-9230 or Pagosa160reconstruction@gmail.com Project Webpage: www.codot.gov/projects/us160pagosasprings
